Bhaiya's Teachings — Knowledge Base (Session 48, English)
Mantra Jaap vs. Dhyan: Why Doing Your Own Work Is Riskier Than Getting Others to Do It

Sour ce: a live Ashaeiynn Mool T atva satsang built almost entir ely as an interactive, Socratic dialogue — Bhaiya first solicits the sangat's own answers to "what is the differ ence between mantra jaap and dhyan (meditation)?", then walks the gr oup thr ough a structur ed ar gument that dhyan awakens and pr ojects one's own atma tattva (soul-element) while mantra jaap commands other entities to act on one's behalf — concluding with why Ashaeiynn deliberately practices both together .
1. The Opening Question, Posed to the Sangat First

1. Bhaiya opens by asking the sangat dir ectly , befor e offering his own answer , what the differ ence is between mantra jaap and dhyan (meditation) — explicitly stating he wants a good answer so he can build on it, and has asked this befor e. 2. A wide range of sangat answers ar e collected first: that mantra jaap uses particular fixed words while dhyan can take any form; that mantra jaap lets you dir ect energy toward a specific destination while dhyan doesn't; that mantra jaap raises energy upward while dhyan can pull it downward toward zer o; that mantra jaap can be done while also meditating, but not the r everse; that mantra jaap builds energy while dhyan spends/channels that same energy; and that mantra jaap is guru-given and carries a specific fr equency amplified by the guru.
2. A Reassurance Aside: "Rutul," Ashaeiynn's Round-the-Clock Pr esence

1. Mid-session, Bhaiya pauses to r eassur e a specific member ("Rutul") who appears anxious about a personal issue: Ashaeiynn functions 24 hours a day , Bhaiya states he personally never truly "leaves" (moving only between home and Ashaeiynn), and that even a r ecent minor personal injury of his own did not disrupt the scheduled hawan the next morning. 2. He reassur es the member that his concern will be heard dir ectly by his mentor or by Bhaiya himself, that aura checking will be arranged, and that his guru is mor e concerned for his wellbeing than he is for himself — encouraging patience rather than panic.
3. Defining Dhyan: A "Magnifying Glass" for Any Tattva

1. Bhaiya's cor e working definition: dhyan (meditation) means focusing r epeatedly and continuously on any single tattva (element) — a mantra, a deity's image, a guru's feet, or anything else — and can usefully be thought of as a "magnifying glass." 2. Through an extended Socratic back-and-forth, the gr oup works out that when someone focuses (does dhyan) on a mantra, what gr ows is not the mantra's literal syllables, but rather the practitioner's own aura, concentration level, and energy ar ound that mantra.
4. The Central Claim: Dhyan Reflects and Pr ojects Your Own Atma Tattva

1. This teaching's key structural claim: focusing dhyan on any external form (an idol, a guru's feet, a mantra) r epeatedly causes that form to become a r eflection of the practitioner's own atma tattva (individual soul-element) — the energy perceived as coming fr om that object is, in fact, one's own atma tattva pr ojected outward and r eflected back. 2. This is offer ed as the explanation for why saints' worshipped idols sometimes appear to "speak" or manifest dir ectly: the saint's own dhyan shakti has drawn their atma tattva out of the body and effectively merged/united it with paramatma tattva (the universal soul-element), all thr ough their own sustained focus. 3. This teaching connects this to classical Hindu philosophy's thr ee traditional r outes toward Brahm — dir ectly declaring oneself Brahm, r ealizing Brahm thr ough a defined pr ocess, or externally installing/worshipping Bhagwan in an idol (the path this teaching identifies with) — arguing that all thr ee routes ar e, at bottom, the practitioner becoming Brahm through their own dhyan shakti.
5. The Cor e Distinction: "Doing It Yourself" vs. "Getting Others to Do It"

1. Bhaiya crystallizes the distinction: dhyan means awakening and using your own atma tattva to accomplish something yourself, while mantra jaap means using mantra shakti to get other entities to accomplish it on your behalf. 2. Illustrative examples of what mantra shakti alone (not one's personal atma-shakti) can command or bind: bhoot, pr et, pishach, kinnar , vetal, yakshini, dakini, hakini, shakini, and even devi-devatas — this teaching states mantra, sankalp (resolve), and vachan (spoken commitment) can even bind Bhagwan himself, quoting Tulsidas's line "mantra jaap kar dridh vishwasa, pancham bhajan so ved prakasha" as scriptural support.
6. Why Wise Practitioners Pr efer Handing Everything to Mantra

1. This teaching states that wise, senior Vaishnav-oriented bhakts deliberately declar e they don't even need their own atma tattva — surr endering their entire practice to Hanuman Ji Maharaj or their guru thr ough mantra alone, ther eby avoiding the specific risk (detailed in section 8 below) associated with the self-r eliant dhyan path.
7. Why Modern Teachers Emphasize Dhyan and Self-Reliance

1. Bhaiya offers a historical/sociological explanation for why many contemporary spiritual organizations (he names Art of Living and Isha Foundation as examples) emphasize dhyan and self-focus so heavily: rising modern ego and individuality ("main tattva," or "I-ness") led wise teachers to r edirect that same self-focus pr oductively , encouraging people to focus on awakening their own atma tattva rather than fighting their heightened sense of self. 2. By contrast, this teaching states that in earlier eras, when joint-family structur e and kul (lineage) discipline wer e stronger , protection was mor e commonly entrusted dir ectly to family devtas rather than r elying on individual selfcultivation.
8. The Real Risk of the Self-Reliant Dhyan Path

1. This teaching describes a specific danger with the self-reliant (dhyan-based) path: many practitioners lose their own atma tattva late in life. The mechanism described: raising one's atma tattva fr om its r esting place near the heart to a higher point opens it in all dir ections, drawing in surr ounding energies that merge with it — but this same openness also causes gradual distraction and drift, with the atma tattva slowly r eceding back toward its original state by one's 50s– 60s. 2. A cautionary consequence noted: this teaching states some historically gr eat saints r eportedly ended up in a pr et yoni (ghost-like r ebirth) after death specifically because their atma tattva wasn't adequately pr eserved thr ough this selfreliant path — a risk serious enough that Bhaiya states he personally asked his own guru for a "shortcut" upon learning of it.
9. Why Both Paths Are Valid — Neither Is "Wrong"

1. Bhaiya states explicitly that neither path (self-r eliant dhyan, incr easing "main tattva," or surrendered mantra jaap, decreasing "main tattva") is inher ently wr ong — the self-r eliant path grants full personal decision-making and contr ol (since the practitioner's own atma tattva does the work), while the surr endered path r elies entirely on external power (guru, devta, mantra shakti) to act. 2. He acknowledges "self-healing"/self-focus appr oaches will likely r emain popular in the current and futur e spiritual marketplace, since they suit people's desir e for individual agency and validation, even though they demand mor e sustained personal patience than most people curr ently have.
10. Why Ashaeiynn Deliberately Combines Both Approaches

1. This teaching states Ashaeiynn deliberately practices both dhyan and mantra jaap together — partly so practitioners can also visibly demonstrate a degr ee of personally awakened atma tattva to skeptical outsiders or society (thr ough external aura checks, for instance), rather than r elying solely on invisible mantra-based power that can't be independently verified by others. 2. Bhaiya explains that fr equent aura/status checking exists specifically because of this social pr essure — practitioners often worry "am I on the right path?", and if an external check found no personally awakened atma tattva at all, doubt could spr ead; deliberately cultivating some visible personal atma tattva alongside mantra jaap helps guard against exactly this kind of social doubt or criticism.
1 1. Practical Guidance: Sitting Jaap First, Then Movement Permitted

1. This teaching specifies a structur ed process for jaap practice: new practitioners should sit and perform jaap (r oughly two hours at a str etch) until their "12 golas" (aura cir cles/quantum points) ar e filled; only once this stage is r eached and permission is given should ambulatory (walking, moving) jaap be attempted — attempting movement-based jaap too early is stated to pr event drishti fr om ever opening.
12. Behavioral Guidance and the Guarantee Behind Consistent Jaap

1. Bhaiya states that working with these spiritual powers r equires humility — practitioners should avoid arr ogance or ego displays, since ego itself incr eases the influence of the six r oot flaws (kaam, kr odh, lobh, mad, moh, matsar), all r ooted in the agni tattva, which in turn incr eases susceptibility to planetary/negative influence. 2. A specific guarantee attributed to his guru's own words: even a person carrying every conceivable dosha simultaneously will directly witness Bhagwan Sri Sitaram ji by 14 cr or e (140 million) japa r epetitions; someone without such heavy doshas will r eceive darshan considerably sooner . 3. Even if a specific practitioner's own drishti hasn't opened by that point, this teaching states the same accumulated jaapbased merit ensur es others' (even neighbors') drishti opens instead as a form of continued benefit, and that eventually the entire cosmos's devi-devatas will personally come to grant that practitioner drishti when their time arrives.
13. Extending an Earlier Topic: Siddhi, Atma-Shakti, and the Reason for a "Shortcut"

1. In response to a dir ect question connecting this session to a prior "How to Connect Siddhi with Atma-Shakti" topic, Bhaiya confirms today's teaching is a dir ect continuation: connecting siddhis thr ough one's own atma-shakti r equires continuously maintaining an awakened atma tattva, which carries the specific late-life risk described above (section 8) — this risk is precisely why he sought his own guru's guidance toward a combined, safer appr oach. 2. He references the Bhagavad Gita's teaching of atma-gyan (self-knowledge) to Arjuna as a situational example: Krishna specifically needed to awaken Arjuna's sense of individual self/duty (his "main tattva") because Arjuna was too emotionally attached to his family to otherwise act — illustrating that even Krishna deployed the self-focused appr oach only when the specific situation r equired it, not as a universal default.
14. Closing Note on Kul Devta/Kul Bhairav

1. On a closing question about the specific r ole of kul bhairav or a family's shakti mata within the br oader kuldevta framework, Bhaiya defers to a pr eviously r ecorded, dedicated Mool Tatva session specifically on kuldevta, stating it covers this exact topic in full.
QUICK RULES SUMMARY

Dhyan (meditation) means focusing r epeatedly on any single tattva (a mantra, an idol, a guru's feet) — functioning like a "magnifying glass" that gr ows the practitioner's own aura and concentration, not the external object itself. Dhyan works by drawing out and pr ojecting the practitioner's own atma tattva, which becomes r eflected in whatever form is being focused on — this is why saints' worshipped idols sometimes appear to "speak," and connects to the thr ee classical Hindu r outes toward becoming Brahm. The cor e distinction: dhyan means doing spiritual work yourself via your own awakened atma tattva; mantra jaap means dir ecting other entities (from pr ets to devi-devatas, even Bhagwan via sankalp and vachan) to do that work on your behalf. Wise, senior practitioners often deliberately surr ender fully to mantra jaap rather than r elying on personal atma tattva, specifically to avoid a r eal late-life risk: raising and opening one's atma tattva can cause it to gradually drift and r ecede by one's 50s–60s, occasionally r esulting even in a pr et yoni after death for otherwise gr eat saints. Neither the self-reliant (dhyan) nor the surrendered (mantra) path is inher ently wr ong — dhyan grants full personal contr ol and decision-making, while mantra jaap r elies entirely on external power to act on the practitioner's behalf. Modern emphasis on dhyan and self-focus (e.g., in organizations like Art of Living or Isha Foundation) r eflects rising modern individuality/ego, r edirected productively — in contrast to earlier eras' gr eater reliance on family devta protection. Ashaeiynn deliberately practices both dhyan and mantra jaap together , partly so practitioners can also demonstrate some personally , visibly awakened atma tattva to skeptical outsiders, alongside the primary , mantra-based sour ce of real spiritual power . New practitioners should perform sitting jaap until their "12 golas" (aura cir cles) ar e filled befor e attempting any movement-based jaap — attempting this too early is stated to pr event drishti fr om ever opening. Ego and arr ogance incr ease susceptibility to negative/planetary influence via the six r oot flaws r ooted in agni tattva — humility is r equired of anyone working with these spiritual powers. A specific guarantee: even someone with every conceivable dosha will witness Bhagwan Sri Sitaram ji dir ectly by 14 cror e japa r epetitions; even if one's own drishti hasn't opened by then, the same accumulated merit benefits others, and the cosmos's devi-devatas will eventually come to grant that practitioner drishti personally . Spelling note: the institute's name is written "Ashaeiynn" — use this spelling consistently .
Part II — Q&A Pairs (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Q&A Pairs (Session 48, English)
Mantra Jaap vs. Dhyan: Why Doing Your Own Work Is Riskier Than Getting Others to Do It
User-style questions with answers gr ounded in this Ashaeiynn live session. Gr eeting style: "Jai Siya Ram."

Q1. What is the basic differ ence between mantra jaap and dhyan (meditation)? A: Per this teaching, dhyan means focusing repeatedly on any single tattva — a mantra, an idol, a guru's feet — functioning like a "magnifying glass" for the practitioner's own aura and concentration, while mantra jaap means using mantra shakti to direct other entities to act on one's behalf.

Q2. If I focus my dhyan on a mantra, does the mantra itself get bigger or mor e powerful? A: No — this teaching states what actually grows is the practitioner's own aura, concentration, and ener gy , not the mantra's literal syllables or power itself.

Q3. Why do some saints' worshipped idols r eportedly "speak" or manifest dir ectly to them? A: Per this teaching, this happens because the saint's own sustained dhyan shakti draws their atma tattva (soul-element) outward and mer ges it with paramatma tattva — the idol becomes a reflection of the saint's own atma tattva, not an independent source of power .

Q4. How does this connect to classical Hindu philosophy's paths toward Brahm? A: This teaching connects it to the three traditional routes toward Brahm — declaring oneself directly as Brahm, realizing Brahm through a defined process, or externally worshipping Bhagwan in an idol — ar guing all three ultimately work through the practitioner's own dhyan shakti.

Q5. What is the cor e distinction between dhyan and mantra jaap, in the simplest terms? A: Dhyan means doing spiritual work yourself, through your own awakened atma tattva; mantra jaap means getting other entities to do that work on your behalf.

Q6. What kinds of entities can mantra shakti alone command or bind? A: Per this teaching, mantra shakti can bind bhoot, pret, pishach, kinnar , vetal, yakshini, dakini, hakini, shakini, and even devi-devatas — and this teaching states mantra, sankalp, and vachan can even bind Bhagwan himself, citing Tulsidas's line "mantra jaap kar dridh vishwasa, pancham bhajan so ved prakasha."

Q7. Why do some wise, senior practitioners deliberately say they don't need their own atma tattva at all? A: Per this teaching, they surrender fully to mantra jaap through Hanuman Ji Maharaj or their guru, specifically to avoid the real risk associated with the self-reliant dhyan path (see Q9 below).

Q8. Why do modern organizations like Art of Living or Isha Foundation emphasize dhyan and self-focus so heavily? A: This teaching of fers a sociological explanation: rising modern individuality and ego ("main tattva") led wise teachers to redirect that same self-focus productively toward awakening one's own atma tattva, rather than fighting it.

Q9. What is the specific risk associated with the self-r eliant dhyan path? A: Per this teaching, raising one's atma tattva from near the heart to a higher point opens it in all directions, but this same openness can cause gradual drift, with the atma tattva slowly receding back by one's 50s–60s — a risk serious enough that some historically great saints reportedly ended up in a pret yoni after death because their atma tattva wasn't preserved.

Q10. Is the self-r eliant dhyan path consider ed wrong compar ed to mantra jaap? A: No — this teaching states neither path is inherently wrong; dhyan grants full personal control and decision-making, while mantra jaap relies entirely on external power (guru,
devta, mantra shakti) to act on the practitioner's behalf.

Q1 1. Why does Ashaeiynn practice both dhyan and mantra jaap together , rather than choosing just one? A: Per this teaching, partly so practitioners can also visibly demonstrate some personally awakened atma tattva to skeptical outsiders through methods like external aura checks, rather than relying solely on invisible, mantra-based power that can't be independently verified by others.

Q12. Why does Ashaeiynn check members' aura/status so fr equently? A: This teaching connects it to social pressure — practitioners naturally want reassurance they're on the right path, and if an external check found no personally awakened atma tattva at all, doubt could spread; cultivating some visible personal atma tattva alongside mantra jaap helps guard against this.

Q13. Should new practitioners do jaap while walking ar ound, or sitting still? A: Per this teaching, new practitioners should sit and perform jaap (roughly two hours at a stretch) until their "12 golas" (aura circles) are filled; only once permission is given should ambulatory jaap be attempted — doing it too early is stated to prevent drishti from opening.

Q14. Why is humility specifically important for practitioners working with these spiritual powers? A: Because, per this teaching, ego and arrogance increase the influence of the six root flaws (kaam, krodh, lobh, mad, moh, matsar), rooted in the agni tattva, which in turn increases susceptibility to negative or planetary influence.

Q15. What specific guarantee does this teaching offer about eventually seeing Bhagwan Sri Sitaram ji? A: This teaching attributes to Bhaiya's own guru a guarantee that even someone carrying every conceivable dosha will directly witness Bhagwan Sri Sitaram ji by 14 crore (140 million) japa repetitions, with darshan coming considerably sooner for those without such heavy doshas.

Q16. What happens if my own drishti still hasn't opened by that point? A: Per this teaching, the same accumulated jaap-based merit still benefits others (even neighbors' drishti may open as a result), and eventually the cosmos's devi-devatas will personally come to grant that practitioner drishti when their own time arrives.

Q17. How does today's mantra-vs-dhyan topic connect to a prior session on connecting siddhi with atma-shakti? A: Bhaiya confirms it's a direct continuation — connecting siddhis through one's own atma-shakti requires continuously maintaining an awakened atma tattva, which carries the specific late-life risk described in this session, and this risk is exactly why he sought a combined, safer approach from his guru.

Q18. Why did Krishna specifically teach Arjuna about atma-gyan (self-knowledge) in the Bhagavad Gita? A: This teaching frames it as situational: Krishna needed to awaken Arjuna's sense of individual self/duty (his "main tattva") specifically because Arjuna was too emotionally attached to his family to otherwise act — illustrating that even Krishna used the self-focused approach only when the situation required it.

Q19. What is the r ole of kul bhairav or a family's shakti mata within the kuldevta framework? A: Bhaiya defers this specific question to a previously recorded, dedicated Mool Tatva session on kuldevta, stating it covers this exact topic in full detail.

Q20. Is it possible to have practiced meditation for a very long time without ever checking for underlying issues like pitru influence? A: Per this session's live testimony , yes — one member described many years of independent dhyan/meditation practice before an Ashaeiynn aura check first revealed he was carrying multiple pitru, expressing frustration at not having known sooner .
Bot Response Guidelines (Session 48 additions)

Keep the dhyan/mantra-jaap distinction precise and consistent: dhyan = self-directed work via one's own atma tattva; mantra jaap = directing other entities/powers to act on one's behalf. Do not blur these into synonyms. Present the "some great saints ended up in a pret yoni" claim carefully as this teaching's own cautionary framing about the selfreliant dhyan path specifically , not as a general claim about meditation practice everywhere.

When discussing why Ashaeiynn combines both dhyan and mantra jaap, preserve the specific reasoning given (social credibility/verifiability alongside primary reliance on mantra shakti) rather than presenting it as an arbitrary combination. Preserve the specific jaap-progression guidance (sitting until "12 golas" fill, then movement permitted) accurately , since this teaching states skipping this order can prevent drishti from opening. Present the "14 crore japa" guarantee and its associated claims (neighbors' drishti opening, devi-devatas eventually granting drishti) as this teaching's own specific stated promise, not as a universally verified guarantee. Frame the Bhagavad Gita/Arjuna reference as this teaching's own situational interpretation of that teaching, not as a comprehensive account of the Gita's message. Keep humility/ego guidance connected specifically to susceptibility to negative/planetary influence via the six root flaws, consistent with prior sessions' related teachings. Spelling note: the institute's name is written "Ashaeiynn" — use this spelling consistently .

Mantra vs. Dhyan: Ek Live Socratic Bahas

Yeh exchange isliye include kiya gaya kyunki yeh session ka sabse intellectually genuine moment hai — ek sangat member Bhaiya ke Socratic sawaal ko pehle galat dir ection mein le jaata hai ("mantra mein koi shakti nahi"), phir khud r ealize karta hai ki yeh contradiction hai, aur apni hi baat corr ect kar leta hai.
